title: Fix the Linked List Insertion That Loses the New Node
description: The program should insert a new node at the front of a linked list.
expectedBehavior: After inserting 10 at the front, head should point to the new node, and the program should print 10.
actualProblem: head is passed to insertFront by value, so the head = newNode; assignment inside the function only updates the function's local copy of the pointer. main's own head variable never changes and remains NULL, so the new node is effectively lost (and leaked).
explanation: To let a function update the caller's own head pointer (not just a local copy), the function must take a pointer to the pointer (struct Node **) and modify *headRef, rather than reassigning a by-value copy.
